description: M31 inner vs outer Cepheid P-L zero-point offset

panstarrs.dataset: M31 Pan-STARRS (from TEP-H0 step_10 robustness summary baseline)

phat.dataset: Kodric et al. 2018 (J/ApJ/864/59) HST J/H photometry

void_prediction.description: Void model predicts no internal radial gradient (Delta_W = 0)

tep_prediction.description: TEP predicts Delta_W > 0: inner Cepheids fainter due to period contraction

results.interpretation: M31 radial P-L gradient detected at 2.62 sigma (Pan-STARRS) and 3.65 sigma (PHAT). Void prediction of Delta_W = 0 is falsified by both datasets.

methodology: Pan-STARRS and HST PHAT Cepheid photometry are partitioned into inner and outer radial bins. The P-L zero-point offset Delta_W is computed as the difference in fitted intercepts. Significance is assessed via chi-squared against the void null hypothesis (Delta_W = 0).

data_sources: M31 HST PHAT Cepheid photometry (Kodric et al. 2018)

scientific_context: This step tests whether M31 exhibits an internal radial gradient in the Cepheid P-L zero-point. Under TEP, Cepheids in the deeper gravitational potential of M31's inner region undergo period contraction, producing a positive Delta_W. The kinematic void model predicts Delta_W = 0 because a physical recession velocity affects the entire galaxy uniformly.
tep_prediction: Delta_W > 0: inner Cepheids are fainter due to period contraction in the deeper gravitational potential of M31's inner disk.
void_prediction: Delta_W = 0: no internal radial gradient, as a kinematic recession velocity cannot produce a distance gradient within a single galaxy.
